name: text

Good morning or afternoon. My project is The Daily Brief, an AI-powered news platform. I will explain the problem it addresses, show how readers and writers use it, and describe how its main parts work together.

name: text
text: Under the Supervision of Prof. Mrinal Kanti Deb Barma, Professor, CSE Department

name: text
text: THE DAILY BRIEF · AI NEWS PLATFORM

This presentation introduces the project and its goals, then walks through the solution, main features, and system design. It ends with the project workflow, current limits, and possible future improvements.

name: text
text: THE DAILY BRIEF · AI NEWS PLATFORM

name: text
text: A website for reading news and sharing articles written by users.

name: text
text: Browse stories from eight categories, popular stories, or search.

name: text
text: Get a short summary or help writing an article.

name: text
text: Follow writers, save stories, listen, like, share, and report concerns.

The Daily Brief is a website where people can read news and publish their own articles. Readers can browse eight topics, search for stories, and see popular articles. AI can summarize a story or help a writer prepare an article. Readers can also follow writers and interact with stories.

name: text
text: THE DAILY BRIEF · AI NEWS PLATFORM

name: text
text: News is spread across websites and topics, so finding a useful story can take time.

name: text
text: Readers may want the main points before reading a full story.

name: text
text: New writers may need help organizing their ideas into an article.

name: text
text: Bring news reading and article writing together in one easy-to-use site.

The project aims to make it easier to find news and understand long stories. It also gives readers a way to become writers. AI tools can help with summaries and article structure, while the writer can edit the final article.

name: text
text: Under the Supervision of Prof. Mrinal Kanti Deb Barma, Professor, CSE Department

name: text
text: THE DAILY BRIEF · AI NEWS PLATFORM

name: text
text: Readers may need to visit several sites to follow different topics.

name: text
text: Long articles can make it harder to quickly understand the main points.

name: text
text: A blank page can make it difficult to organize a news article.

name: text
text: Harmful content and inaccurate claims need careful review.

The project focuses on four challenges: finding stories across topics, understanding long articles, helping people start writing, and reviewing content. The platform provides tools for these needs, while recognizing that automated checks cannot confirm every fact.

name: text

The Daily Brief brings news stories and reader-written articles together. Readers can ask AI for a summary and use the listen feature. Writers can start with a topic or a full draft, edit the result, add an image, and send it for review.

This slide compares broad product types, not specific companies. The Daily Brief combines category-based news browsing with AI summaries and reader articles. A traditional news website often focuses on news from its own newsroom. A writing tool usually focuses on drafting text. The features offered by individual services can differ.

name: text
text: AI and news services used by the website

Readers use the website to browse news and community articles. The website reads and saves information in MongoDB. It also sends requests to OpenAI for summaries, writing help, and content checks. A news feed provides links that appear by topic.

text: THE DAILY BRIEF · AI NEWS PLATFORM

name: text
text: Next.js and React build the pages people use.

name: text
text: Handles sign-in, search, article writing, and reader actions.

name: text
text: MongoDB stores accounts, news links, articles, and activity.

name: text
text: OpenAI supports summaries and writing; browser speech reads articles aloud.

The project uses Next.js and React for the website. Server code handles sign-in, search, article writing, and reader actions. MongoDB stores accounts and articles, and GridFS stores uploaded images. OpenAI provides AI features, and the browser reads articles aloud.

name: text

This is the basic user journey. A reader browses or searches for news, opens a story, and can ask for a summary. The reader may save or share it, or follow its writer. Someone who wants to publish can create and edit an article, then submit it for screening and, when needed, admin review.

name: text
text: AI organizes a draft or writes a first version.

name: text
text: For topic writing, search runs only if AI needs more facts.

name: text
text: Review the headline, topic, article, and image.

name: text
text: Safety check; admin reviews flagged or unavailable cases.

name: text
text: Approved articles appear for readers and in search.

A writer starts with either a full article draft or a topic. For topic writing, the system checks whether AI already knows enough; it searches only when more information is needed. The writer edits the article and image before submitting. Safety checks run, and an admin reviews cases that need a person. Approved posts become visible to readers.

name: text
text: The home page combines news links and articles written by users.

name: text
text: Some article topics need fresh information from the web.

name: text
text: Text and images need screening, with people to review uncertain cases.

name: text
text: Accounts, posts, images, and reader actions need reliable storage.

The project needed to bring different kinds of stories together. Some topics need fresh information. Posts and images need safety checks, and uncertain submissions need human review. The database also needs to keep user accounts and article activity.

name: text
text: THE DAILY BRIEF · AI NEWS PLATFORM

name: text
text: News links and community articles appear in topic pages and search.

name: text
text: AI checks its knowledge before deciding whether to use web search.

name: text
text: AI screens text and images; admins decide cases needing review.

name: text
text: MongoDB stores posts and reader activity; images use GridFS.

The project uses shared topic categories for different story types and includes community stories in search. For AI writing, it checks model knowledge before using web search. It screens article text and images, then sends uncertain content to an admin. MongoDB stores user and article data, and GridFS stores images.

text: THE DAILY BRIEF · AI NEWS PLATFORM

name: text
text: Content screening does not prove that every statement is true.

name: text
text: A flag count shows concern, not whether a claim is false.

name: text
text: Writers should review and edit generated content before publishing.

name: text
text: AI, database, and news feed features depend on other services.

The current safety system looks for harmful content but does not check every claim against evidence. Reader reports are signals that something may need review. AI can also make mistakes, so writers should edit drafts before publishing. Some features rely on external services being available.

name: text

name: text

name: text
text: Show sources that support or challenge important claims.

Future versions could create a relevant image from an article topic, recommend related stories, and improve image checks. Image checks could look for harmful content, misleading edits, or text inside an image. Another goal is to compare important claims with reliable sources and show readers the evidence.

The Daily Brief combines news discovery, AI reading and writing tools, and community publishing. Readers can follow writers and interact with stories. Safety checks and admin review help manage submissions. Future work can improve source checks and image tools.
